messages:
Marya: Quick check — customer ACME (private VPC) reports weird gaps in their Grafana dashboards and a bunch of CPU alert noise. They're using grafana-agent -> Prom remote_write into our peering. Where should I point them for the canonical dashboards + logs? Also who can advise on tuning the node/instance CPU alert thresholds?

Josh: Point them to the customer overview dash first: https://grafana.internal.redwood/d/abcd1234/customer-acme-overview?orgId=1 — that shows node + pod CPU, request rates, and remote_write status panel.

Liz: For logs, check Loki under k8s cluster label. Example query: `{cluster=\"acme-prod\", app=\"otel-collector\"} |= \"error\"` — Grafana Explore -> Loki. If grafana-agent is used, search for `agent_remote_write` logs in the agent pod.

Marya: thx. Any quick kubectl commands I can hand their infra team to verify remote_write connectivity from their side?

Josh: sure — share these two:
```
# check grafana-agent pod logs
kubectl -n observability logs -l app=grafana-agent -c agent --tail=200 | grep remote_write
# check remote_write metrics on their side (if they run prom)
curl -g 'http://localhost:9090/api/v1/query?query=rate(prometheus_remote_storage_samples_sent_total[5m])'
```

Liz: Also share this PromQL they can run from our side (Grafana Explore -> Prometheus datasource):
```
rate(prometheus_remote_storage_samples_failures_total{job=~\"agent|remote_write\"}[5m])
```

DanOps: For alert tuning — the CPU alert currently triggers at 85% sustained 5m. For these VPC-onprem customers we usually bump to 90% or change to 15m window to avoid churn during autoscaling. I can open a PR in infra/alert-rules to add `labels: {ticket: \"support-<id>\"}` and a `for: 15m` for acme-specific override.

Marya: Perfect. If we change to 15m do we risk missing real incidents?

DanOps: Slightly higher risk for short spikes, but these look like churn from node drains during maintenance. We can also add an alert suppression rule tied to k8s annotation `redwood/maintenance=true`. That keeps signal while reducing noise.

Liz: FYI the OTEL collector for ACME has been flapping (OOMKill) last night — logs show `failed to flush batch` from otlp exporter. If they switch to smaller batch_size and enable retry_on_failure it stabilizes. Putting the snippet here: 
```
exporters:
  otlp:
    endpoint: \"https://otlp-ingest.redwood.internal:4317\"
    compression: on
    retry_on_failure:
      enabled: true
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      exporters: [otlp]
```

Marya: Can you add that to the onboarding checklist? I'll send it to the customer.

Liz: Yep, adding now. Will link the checklist page: https://docs.redwood.internal/obs/private-vpc-agent-setup

observability-bot: deploy-bot: Noted — alert-rules PR template opened by DanOps: infra/alert-rules#456 (canary).

Marya: Thanks all. I'll ping ACME with the grafana link, kubectl commands, and the OTEL config snippet. DanOps — assign me the PR for follow-up once it's ready. :thumbsup:

DanOps: assigned. I'll also add a short runbook block for `silence during node drain` and post it to the runbooks channel.

Marya: Awesome — closing this mini-check. If anything else pops up I'll re-open here.
